name: Time Machine
description: One place, more than one life. Turn an illustrated dial and watch the architecture change around a registered viewpoint.

compatibility: A WebGL2 scene with an included Three.js runtime in the standalone export. A labeled static drawing remains available without JavaScript or WebGL2.
Dial, slider, era buttons and keyboard control the same reversible timeline. Touch dragging operates the dial and the optional orbit camera.
Reduced motion uses immediate manual changes and disables automatic playback. Paused, settled, hidden and offscreen studies stop rendering.
One renderer draws both comparison panels using the same camera transform. Narrow screens stack the registered views vertically.

All building arrangements and eras are fictional. The optional Tampa-inspired preset is not a historical reconstruction. The undated reference photo is an artistic surface collage, not evidence of any era.
notes: Time is sampled from ordered object keyframes independently of rendering. Walls change height, roofs change pitch, window frames assemble by floor, and a chimney, trees and canopy change in the same coordinate system.

Every intermediate time is deterministic and reversible. Geometry and object identities persist during time changes. Construction lines trace the changing extents rather than fading between whole-scene photographs.
The registered camera is independent of time. Orbit is an explicit inspection mode; Lock viewpoint restores the original camera. Both comparison panels use the same view transform.
Photo mode combines a registered reference surface and three original survey layers. The facade texture follows the same local wall coordinates while the map planes retain fixed world coordinates.
The neutral sample and optional Tampa-inspired block use conceptual periods called Workshop, Exchange and Common ground. They do not assert historical dates, street layouts or building histories.

The location schema accepts eras, geometry, custom triangle morphs, material keyframes, media layers and spatial annotations. Documented records require source URLs; artistic reconstructions and fictional data retain separate labels.
reuse: Serve the source ZIP over local HTTP and open example.html. It includes settings, the instrument, photographs, surveys and the exact Three.js runtime/license.
Use createTimeScene for a render-independent registered scene, createTimeViewer for a canvas, or mount for the complete dial and controls. A custom location can be supplied to each API.
Read README.md for time-keyed object and media schemas, custom geometry, coordinate alignment, provenance and lifecycle. No Tampa routing or Stories modules are required.
Keep photo licenses and factual provenance attached to their assets. The sample coordinates are arbitrary scene units, not geographic coordinates.
